text: "Approve as drafted (Recommended)": record the approval, run a 2-request-per-tier smoke on each model to confirm the wiring, then run the full baseline as a systemd --user unit and write replay-baseline.json (owner, 2026-11-13, answering: OpenCode Go; muse-spark-1.3-contributor, deepseek-v4.1-flash and mimo-v2.6-flash; 108 requests per model; package defaults; 8,192 output tokens; about 1.5M input tokens per model; a hard stop at 3M input tokens per model; the four decision rules fixed and hashed).
modelsBasis: the plan default: gate M-2 workers (muse-spark-1.3-contributor, deepseek-v4.1-flash) and its S1 model (mimo-v2.6-flash), on OpenCode Go (owner, 2026-11-12, owner-gate-m2.json)
workerSettings: package defaults (resolveMemorySystemConfig({})): thinkingLevel low for STM and WM, wm.targetRatio 0.2, wm.batchTokens 3,000; one pass per request; the flush output-cap retry for WM

estimate.basis: the 2026-11-13 smoke (2 STM + 2 WM requests per model on persona ls10): STM about 15-19K input tokens per request by the provider's count; WM 6-47K per request (DeepSeek re-sends the verdicts the 32-call turn limit refuses over 2-4 turns); long-scope adds about 4-5K tokens per turn
estimate.costBasis: input tokens x $0.065 per 1M (the plan all-in Muse rate); OpenCode Go bills a subscription

runs.baseline: docs/_evidence/memory-bench/218.2/replay-baseline.json: the current product, before Task 2 lands
runs.after: docs/_evidence/memory-bench/218.2/replay-after.json: the product after Tasks 2-7, same models and fixture hash (Task 9)
runs.task2: docs/_evidence/memory-bench/218.2/replay-task2.json: the STM tier alone (--only stm --label task2) on the product with Task 2's fields, same models, fixture hash, rules and ceiling; decides Task 2's rule against the baseline
runs.task4: docs/_evidence/memory-bench/218.2/replay-task4.json: the STM tier alone (--only stm --label task4) on the product with Task 4's automatic evidence chunk (stm.autoChunkBytes 1024), same models, fixture hash, rules and ceiling; decides Task 4's rule against the baseline
runs.task6: docs/_evidence/memory-bench/218.2/replay-task6.json: the 24 long-scope WM requests alone (--only wm --set long-scope --scope-digest --label task6) on the product with judge and the scope digest (minBytes 8,192, maxBytes 2,048), same models, fixture hash, rules and ceiling; decides Task 6's rule against replay-task5-judge.json

task2.text: The English patterns (CORRECTION, FAILED_VERIFICATION, FAILED_OUTCOME) are removed, with no alias, if on every worker model, for both the correction and the failure signal, the fields' recall is at least the patterns' on the English cases and higher on the non-English cases, with precision (all cases) no lower; otherwise they are kept as a union with the fields for records that carry no field. Output tokens per event may rise by at most 15% against the baseline; a larger rise goes to the owner with the counts.

task4.text: The automatic evidence chunk ships on by default if, on every worker model, annotated-evidence coverage rises against the baseline and chunk store bytes per 10k source tokens stay under 2x the baseline; otherwise it ships off and the counts go to the owner.

task5.text: judge replaces keep, summarize, derive and discard if, on every worker model, the share of records given a verdict is no lower, annotated later-step records kept and changed values kept are no lower, and output tokens per record fall by at least 30% or refused calls fall. Otherwise judge is deleted and the settled-first step ships alone when it passes the first two conditions.

task6.text: wm.scopeDigest defaults on only if, on the long-scope set, annotated later-step records kept rise on at least one worker model and fall on none; otherwise its code is deleted and the counts recorded.

ruleChange: a rule changed after the baseline is refused (assertRulesUnchanged): the baseline records the rules hash it ran under

changes.change: maxInputTokensPerModel 3,000,000 -> 4,000,000 before the baseline: the smoke projected deepseek-v4.1-flash at about 2.9M input tokens. Only the safety stop changed; models, fixture and rules are unchanged and nothing had been scored.

An added run, replay-task2.json: the 60 STM requests on the same three models, fixture hash, rules (hash unchanged) and per-model ceiling, on the product with Task 2's record_event fields, so Task 2's rule is decided in Task 2. Estimated 0.6-1M input tokens per model (the STM share of the baseline). Models, fixture and rules are unchanged.

An added run, replay-task4.json: the 60 STM requests on the same three models, fixture hash, rules (hash unchanged) and per-model ceiling, on the product with Task 4's automatic evidence chunk, so Task 4's rule is decided in Task 4. Estimated 0.6-1M input tokens per model (Task 2's STM run). Models, fixture and rules are unchanged.

Owner decision after replay-task4.json: Task 4's rule (fixed, hash unchanged) said off because muse-spark-1.3-contributor's chunk bytes per 10k source tokens (188) passed 2x its baseline (74); coverage rose on all three models. The owner overrides the outcome, not the rule: stm.autoChunkBytes defaults to 1024.

Two added runs, replay-task5-incumbent.json (--only wm --wm-format tools: the four tools on the current product) and replay-task5-judge.json (--only wm --wm-format judge --settle-first), so Task 5's rule is decided in Task 5 against an incumbent on the same product (Task 3's protections changed the WM requests since the baseline). Same three models, fixture hash, rules (hash unchanged) and per-model ceiling. Recorded after the runs: the plan's Task 5 text names the --wm-format comparison, and no owner prompt preceded them. Input tokens: incumbent 0.73M / 0.92M / 1.00M, judge 0.74M / 0.46M / 0.46M (Muse / DeepSeek / MiMo).
changes.text: Plan 218.2 Task 5 ("Build judge, measure it against the incumbent on the worker replay, and delete the loser")

changes.change: Owner decision after replay-task5-judge.json: Task 5's rule (fixed, hash unchanged) said judge loses, on one check only: deepseek-v4.1-flash kept 89 of 96 annotated later-step records against the incumbent's 90 (the same format gave 93 in the baseline). Verdict share, changed values kept and output tokens per record (-35% / -67% / -55%) passed on every model. The owner overrides the outcome, not the rule: judge replaces keep, summarize, derive and discard. Later-step records discarded rose (Muse 0 -> 11, MiMo 0 -> 9, DeepSeek 4 -> 3) and are carried to Task 9's replay.

An added run, replay-task6.json: the 24 long-scope WM requests on the same three models, fixture hash, rules (hash unchanged) and per-model ceiling, with the scope digest on (one digest call per scope hash and model), so Task 6's rule is decided in Task 6 against replay-task5-judge.json (the plan's amendment of 2026-11-15). Estimated 0.25-0.4M input tokens per model. Models, fixture and rules are unchanged.
